before_start: Use tasks.json as the source of truth for task status and dependency selection.
Use taskos claim before implementation to atomically claim one dependency-ready task.
Read ROADMAP.md and the relevant canonical docs when choosing product direction.
before_finish: Run focused checks for the changed area.
Use taskos done/block/release to update task status and progress.
Do not manually edit generated task views.

tasks.title: Establish Python bot foundation
tasks.description: Create the aiogram/SQLAlchemy project skeleton, local runtime files, configuration layer, and application entry point.
scope: Docker Compose and local PostgreSQL scaffolding
acceptance_criteria: The bot can be started with python -m app.main after env setup
Runtime configuration comes from environment variables
Handlers receive a managed async database session
tasks.notes: Implemented before TaskOS adoption.

tasks.title: Build core database schema and migrations
tasks.description: Define the MVP data model and Alembic migrations for users, couples, tasks, shopping, content, notifications, aliases, chat blocks, and places.
acceptance_criteria: All core tables are registered
MVP shared entities remain scoped through ownership and couple membership
Migrations support local and container startup
tasks.notes: Direct couple_id fields are intentionally deferred for a later scale migration.

tasks.title: Implement couple onboarding and invite codes
tasks.description: Allow users to create or join a two-person couple space with readable invite codes and safe onboarding states.
scope: Expired, invalid, full, and already-in-couple cases
acceptance_criteria: A user can create a couple and a partner can join
Invalid or expired invite codes are handled softly
A user cannot join multiple couples
tasks.notes: Current MVP is optimized for one real couple while keeping multi-couple architecture possible.

tasks.title: Implement Telegram main menu and recovery flows
tasks.description: Provide compact Telegram-native navigation, recoverable screens, and smart cleanup of old bot blocks.
acceptance_criteria: Users without a couple are blocked from protected menus
Users in a couple can always return to a safe menu
Old screens are closed or cleaned up predictably
tasks.notes: The UX should stay compact and non-corporate.

tasks.title: Add partner display names
tasks.description: Let each user define a gentle display name for their partner and use those names in cards and notifications.
scope: Alias normalization and fallback display names
Alias usage in task cards and notifications
acceptance_criteria: Aliases are trimmed and length-limited
Fallback names work when an alias is missing
Task notifications and cards show partner-friendly names
tasks.notes: Implemented in migration 0002 and partner alias service.

tasks.title: Implement household tasks and recurrence
tasks.description: Support shared household tasks, assignments, a task pool, completion, archiving, and recurring task regeneration.
scope: Task creation and assignment to self, partner, or pool
Daily, weekly, monthly, and custom recurrence
acceptance_criteria: Partner-assigned tasks notify the partner
Pool tasks can be claimed and completed
Recurring tasks create exactly one next occurrence
Tasks from another couple are not exposed
tasks.notes: Custom recurrence interval support is included.

tasks.title: Implement shared shopping list
tasks.description: Support a calm shared shopping list where active and bought items are visible until local midnight cleanup.
acceptance_criteria: Items can be added and marked bought
Bought items are archived after the couple's local midnight
The panel keeps active items first
tasks.notes: Partner notifications are intentionally deferred.

tasks.title: Implement content tracker
tasks.description: Track shared movies, series, books, games, and other content with completion, ratings, reactions, comments, and filters.
scope: Status, category, rating, and date filters
acceptance_criteria: Content can be added, completed, rated, and commented
Both partners can comment
Filters respect status, category, rating, and couple timezone
tasks.notes: Current content feature is stronger than the original bare MVP.

tasks.title: Implement places tracker
tasks.description: Track places the couple wants to visit, mark them visited, and store ratings and comments.
acceptance_criteria: Places can be added, visited, rated, and commented
Rating and comments require a visited place
Lists separate planned and visited places
tasks.notes: Filters and partner notifications are deferred.

tasks.title: Implement statistics and recaps
tasks.description: Provide weekly and monthly summaries that cover completed tasks, content, ratings, overdue work, and cozy recap copy.
acceptance_criteria: Weekly and monthly periods use the couple timezone
Monthly recap handles the first day of a month correctly
Recap text remains compact and warm
tasks.notes: Shopping and places are not deeply represented yet.

tasks.title: Implement scheduler and reminders
tasks.description: Run background jobs for recurring task regeneration, shopping cleanup, and scheduled couple notifications with dedupe keys.
acceptance_criteria: Due recurring tasks regenerate once
Scheduled notifications are sent once per local period
Reminder timing uses the couple timezone
tasks.notes: APScheduler is enough for the MVP; Redis/Celery is deferred.

tasks.title: Add cozy AI suffixes and local cat assets
tasks.description: Make notifications warmer through optional OpenAI suffixes and local cat images, while retaining deterministic fallbacks.
scope: Fallback cozy messages without API key
acceptance_criteria: Missing OPENAI_API_KEY does not break notifications
Generated suffixes are short and sanitized
Missing cat assets fall back to plain text
tasks.notes: The cozy layer should stay subtle.

tasks.title: Prepare local deployment scaffolding
tasks.description: Make the MVP runnable locally through Docker Compose and ready for single-process polling deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Docker Compose waits for database health
Entrypoint applies migrations before starting the bot
README documents local and MVP deployment notes
tasks.notes: Full production finalization remains pending.

tasks.title: Establish tests and architecture guardrails
tasks.description: Cover the implemented MVP behavior with focused tests and protect the handlers-services-repositories boundary.
acceptance_criteria: The full test suite passes
Handlers do not import repositories or embed SQL
Core product flows are covered by tests
tasks.notes: Current suite has 85 passing tests.

tasks.title: Adopt Codex TaskOS planning loop
tasks.description: Install TaskOS, configure project task files, and generate a kanban/dashboard from the project roadmap.
acceptance_criteria: taskos doctor passes
taskos validate passes
Generated boards reflect tasks.json
tasks.notes: Completed in this workspace on 2026-05-22.

tasks.title: Choose production target and release checklist
tasks.description: Decide where the MVP will run first and write the concrete release checklist for credentials, migration, polling safety, and smoke testing.
scope: Pick Railway, Render, or VPS as the first production target
List required environment variables and secret handling
Define database provisioning and migration steps
Explicitly support using the bot when the local Docker stack is turned off
acceptance_criteria: ROADMAP.md and README identify the chosen target
Release checklist is concrete enough to execute
No secrets are committed
tasks.notes: User-requested rank 1: make the bot available from a server instead of depending on local Docker.

tasks.title: Finalize production deployment
tasks.description: Deploy the bot and database to the selected production platform, run migrations, and verify the first real polling instance.
scope: Build and run the bot container
Verify onboarding and main menu with the real bot token
acceptance_criteria: Production bot runs as a single polling process
Database migrations are applied
Smoke test confirms onboarding, menu, task creation, and reminder-safe startup
The bot remains available when the local Docker stack is stopped
test_steps: docker compose run --rm bot python -m alembic upgrade head
ssh BatchMode check reached server and returned publickey/password required
VPS docker compose ps: bot up, db healthy
tasks.notes:
Blocked until a production platform, database, bot token, and deployment credentials are selected. This is the execution half of user-requested rank 1.
VPS target is chosen, but noninteractive SSH deploy needs key-based root access. Password must not be embedded in commands or files; add an SSH public key or run the first login step manually.
SSH key access to VPS has been confirmed.
